I've been doing this for 25 years on this same land. I know what this soil needs and what I can manage with my family's situation — two of my kids are working in the city now, so I can't always count on extra hands at peak time. I have to be practical.

For **wheat**, I'll plant in mid-October once I finish harvesting the maize. I'll do rotary tillage to break up the stubble and then sow a local improved variety — I've been using the same type for years and the yield is reliable. I'm not going to try some new experimental variety. I'll apply base fertilizer before planting — mostly compound fertilizer plus a top-dress of urea at jointing. Wheat needs water badly at jointing and heading, so I'll pump the well at least 4 times this season. I'll spray herbicide in early spring and hit it once more if powdery mildew shows up. I'm expecting around 450 jin per mu — that's been my average.

For **summer maize**, I'll plant right after the wheat comes off in June, no time to waste. I'll use a hybrid seed like Zhengdan 958 or similar — everyone around here does, it yields well. I'll use a seeder to plant directly into the stubble with rotary tillage. Maize is heavy on nitrogen so I'll apply a good base dose and top-dress again at the big bell stage. I'll irrigate at planting if it's dry, then at tasseling, then watch grain fill. Two pesticide passes — one herbicide early, one for corn borer if needed. I expect about 550 jin per mu.

Between the off-farm income and what I grow, the family gets by. I don't gamble on new methods. I do what works.
